q: What is the path back below 60% cost-to-income and above 12% ROE?

r.narrative: Comparable cost-to-income is **62.6% year-to-date (66% in Q3)** and the 9+3 forecast is **63.2%**, and ROE is **12.7%** — but only **11.0%** with normal credit losses (targets: CIR < 60%, ROE > 12%). The path back needs about **€11.3M more income and €6.5M less cost**: AUM +5% (+€3.5M fees), 12-month Euribor +25 bp as the group hedges roll (+€6.0M NII), a 3% MOPS commission price-list change (+€1.8M), the Oracle decommission (−€2.0M), a purchased-services and marketing cap (−€3.0M) and holding 15 open positions (−€1.5M). Result: **CIR 58.7% and ROE 14.9% (13.3% with credit losses back at 20 bps)**, with credit losses planned at a normal 20 bps.

q: Why is Q3 opex above budget? Show the Basware invoices behind it

r.narrative: Comparable opex is **€136.0M year-to-date against €131.6M budget (+€4.4M)**. q: How did income perform year-to-date vs budget — NII, commissions and life insurance?

q: What do Euribor −50bp and AUM +5% do to 2027 income, CIR and ROE?

r.narrative: On the 2027 roll-forward of the 9+3 forecast: **12-month Euribor −50 bp costs about €8.0M of NII** as household and housing-company loans reset and deposit margins after FTP shrink (the hedge book softens year one). **AUM +5% adds about €3.5M** of fund and mandate fees at a 0.42% blended fee rate. Combined, income falls **€4.5M**, comparable CIR rises **from 63.2% to 64.2%** and ROE falls **from 12.7% to 12.2%**. AUM growth alone takes CIR down 0.7 points and uses almost no capital.

q: Why are credit losses a release this year, and what should we plan for Q4?

r.narrative: Credit losses are a **€3.5M net release year-to-date** against a **€12.3M charge in the budget** and €15.8M in FY2025. The release comes from **stage 3** (two individually assessed corporate cases resolved, +€2.9M), **stage 1/2 model ECL** (house prices stabilised, +€1.6M) and a partial release of the **construction overlay** (+€0.4M), net of new charges on consumer loans and cards (−€1.4M). It is not a run-rate: a normal year for Aktia is 15–20 bps on a €7.9bn book. **Plan Q4 at about €5.0M** (20 bps annualised) and 2027 at €14–16M.
r.sql:
SELECT MOVEMENT_TYPE, SUM(MOVEMENT_EUR_M) AS ytd_eur_m
FROM SDP_AKTIA.PUBLIC.AKTIA_ECL_MOVEMENT
WHERE PERIOD BETWEEN '2026-01' AND '2026-09'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;

q: Could the platform also cover consolidation — what would eliminations and the Workiva feed look like?

r.narrative: **Exploratory** — Aktia has not decided to replace its consolidation system. The group is simple to consolidate: three main entities, all in euros, with about **€11.5M a year of eliminations**. Distribution commissions from Aktia Fund Management (€6.1M) and Aktia Life Insurance (€2.8M) to the bank and service recharges from the bank (€2.6M) are matched by counterparty and account in Snowflake; about **96% would auto-match** in a proof of concept. The consolidated P&L, balance sheet and segment tables would be published as governed views that **feed Workiva**, which stays the reporting layer.
r.sql:
SELECT FROM_ENTITY, TO_ENTITY, FLOW_TYPE, SUM(AMOUNT_EUR_M) AS fy_eur_m
FROM SDP_AKTIA.PUBLIC.AKTIA_IC_ELIMINATIONS
WHERE FISCAL_YEAR = 2025
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ORDER BY 4 DESC;

r.narrative:
**Draft CFO commentary — Q3 2026** (published figures; plan data synthetic)

**Headline.** Comparable operating profit was €84.8M for January–September, €0.9M behind budget and 3% above last year. The full year is in line with the outlook of about €106M.

**Efficiency.** Comparable cost-to-income was 62.6% year-to-date and 66% in Q3, above the target of below 60%. The 9+3 forecast is 63.2%; ROE is 12.7%, but 11.0% with normal credit losses, against a target above 12%.

**Income.** Operating income was €217.4M (−€12.2M vs budget). NII was €97.0M: financing costs rose and group hedges delay the benefit of higher market rates into 2027. Commissions were €96.0M (+4% y/y) on record AUM of €18.2bn and €124M of Q3 net sales. Life insurance was €20.9M as the run-off book was hit by rising rates.

**Costs.** Comparable opex was €136.0M (+6% y/y, +€4.4M vs budget): IT, personnel, purchased services and marketing.

**Credit.** Credit losses were a €3.5M net release. This supports profit this year but does not fix the cost-to-income gap; Q4 is planned at a normal €5.0M charge.

**Capital.** CET1 12.6%, 4.0 points above the minimum. S&P raised the outlook to stable on 28 October.

**Actions for 2027.** (1) Set the Oracle decommission date (−€2.0M); (2) cap purchased services and marketing (−€3.0M); (3) plan the MOPS commission price list +3% (+€1.8M); (4) plan AUM growth of 5% (+€3.5M). Together with the hedge roll-off these bring CIR to about 58.7% and ROE to 14.9% (13.3% with normal credit losses).
